title: CFOs Meet LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2606.13812v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Business sentiment is a closely watched economic signal, but measuring it is slow and costly: surveys typically reach only a few hundred firms, arrive periodically, and take time to compile. We show that large language models hold the potential to address these shortcomings. We prompt an LLM to role-play as the CFO of a specific company on a specific date, for every public-company CFO who responded to the Duke--Federal Reserve CFO Survey between 2002 and 2025, and answer a question about economy-wide optimism. The LLM-generated optimism score predicts the individual CFO's actual answer, even in specifications that include firm and year-quarter fixed effects as well as a control variable measuring the human CFO's lagged response. Accuracy increases with the information provided to the LLM, and the relation persists under quarterly aggregation. translated_abstract: 商业情绪是备受关注的经济信号，但对其进行测量既缓慢又成本高昂：调查通常仅覆盖几百家公司，按周期发布，且编制需要时间。我们证明大语言模型有潜力解决这些不足。我们让大语言模型扮演特定公司在特定日期的首席财务官（CFO）角色——针对2002年至2025年间回应杜克-美联储CFO调查的每一位上市公司CFO——并回答一个关于整体经济乐观程度的问题。由LLM生成的乐观程度评分能够预测该CFO的实际回答，即使在包含公司固定效应、年-季度固定效应以及衡量人类CFO滞后回答的对照变量的回归设定下依然如此。随着提供给LLM的信息增多，准确性随之提高，且这种关系在季度加总后依然存在。我们发现，在衡量CFO预期的另外两个问题上也存在相同的模式。（注：原文摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 让大语言模型扮演CFO角色生成的乐观评分能够准确预测真实CFO的调查回答，为快速、低成本地测量商业情绪提供了新途径。
en_tdlr: LLM-generated optimism scores, produced by having LLMs role-play as CFOs, accurately predict actual CFO survey responses, offering a fast and low-cost new approach to measuring business sentiment.
